tasks.short: Encourage exploration and perseverance for later grades

steps.what: Discuss students’ interests, challenges and possible learning opportunities
Encourage students to explore opportunities and persevere with challenging tasks

tasks.design: Keep encouragement and exploration conversations with the teacher. The design introduces no motivation score or automated counselling substitute.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful encouragement depends on trust and understanding why a learner is struggling.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability establishes an equivalent replacement for this interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a productive challenge from a barrier that needs support.
tasks.human_edge: Show confidence in the student while listening to their concerns.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains mentoring responsibility and direct contact.

reach.task: Discuss learning barriers requiring wider support
reach.learn: Recognise when encouragement alone is insufficient

evidence.claim: Encouragement and learner support depend on contextual dialogue; drafting motivational text is not equivalent work.

assumptions: Teacher elicits perspectives and observes barriers in s1; no structured motivation or emotional-state feed is assumed.
Learning-opportunity information comes from existing school materials and staff; no new directory is created.
No new application or process means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Which learning opportunities are actually available to pupils
research_questions: Which barriers need practical support rather than more encouragement?

incremental.description: No new mentoring application or data flow

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=40+60=100. Listening and encouragement remain unchanged, with no presumed reduction in learner contact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach subjects through lectures, discussions and demonstrations

steps.what: Orient students to the subject and explain the lesson’s learning purpose
Instruct through lectures, discussions and demonstrations and respond to student understanding

tasks.design: Keep live subject teaching with the teacher, using existing approved materials in {LMS}. Preparation assistants may support a separate preparation task; they do not reduce classroom teaching time in this design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instruction requires interpretation of student responses and interactive explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest describes preparation support, which does not establish replacement of live instruction.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise misconceptions and choose an effective explanation in the moment.
tasks.human_edge: Draw students into discussion and respond to their reasoning.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time, authority and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Observe and discuss subject teaching methods
reach.learn: Use student responses to revise explanations

evidence.claim: The secondary-school study described in the digest concerns reduced lesson preparation, not reduced time delivering lectures or discussions.

assumptions: The existing lesson plan and approved materials are created during preparation tasks, whose effort is not repeated or credited here.
Teacher establishes readiness through interaction; no automated understanding feed is assumed.
No new teaching system or maintenance is introduced.
unknowns: Which subjects, class sizes and demonstration constraints apply
research_questions: Which student responses most often require the teacher to change the explanation?

incremental.description: No additional classroom system to maintain

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=15+85=100. Live instruction stays unchanged; preparation savings from another task or study are not imported.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish and enforce classroom behavior rules

steps.what: Establish behavior rules and explain procedures for maintaining order among students
Observe behavior and enforce rules with proportionate responses and clarification

tasks.design: Keep classroom rule setting and responses with the teacher, aligned with school policy in {DOCS}. No behavior classifier, emotion inference or automatic sanction is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fair responses require understanding context and individual explanations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing policy and direct communication remain sufficient for this design.
tasks.human_edge: Build a classroom climate where pupils understand expectations and can explain difficulties.
tasks.altitude: The teacher retains rule-setting and intervention responsibilities.

reach.learn: Separate observed conduct from inferred motives

evidence.claim: Establishing and applying classroom rules depends on interpersonal and contextual judgement.

assumptions: School administration supplies current policy; teacher develops and explains classroom procedures in s1.
Teacher directly observes and clarifies events in s2; no structured violation codes are assumed.
Formal record maintenance is separate. No new tool or workflow creates upkeep.
unknowns: Which classroom decisions require administrator escalation
research_questions: Do pupils understand the procedures and know how to ask for clarification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100; R=30+70=100. Rule development, explanation and proportionate response retain time; no automated discipline saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt teaching methods and instructional materials

steps.what: Identify students’ varying needs and choose the instructional adaptation required
Rewrite instructional materials at the chosen level while preserving subject meaning

loop.purpose: Draft a teacher-requested alternative wording or scaffold
loop.input: Source material and nonidentifying teacher adaptation brief
loop.check: Teacher compares source and draft for factual accuracy, preserved concepts, reading suitability and whether scaffolding still requires the intended learning
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; teacher rewrites rejected passages
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse existing approved alternatives first; a new level-specific rewrite requires semantic language transformation

steps.what: Approve adapted materials and adjust teaching methods as students use them

tasks.design: Use the approved native editor in {LMS} or {DOCS} to draft the teacher-specified material adaptation. The teacher checks meaning before use and retains all decisions about needs, methods and the response to student learning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing alternate wording can be time-consuming after the teacher has decided what needs changing.
tasks.enabler_now: Teaching editors already offer level changes, summaries and translation.
tasks.still_hard: Preserve disciplinary meaning and avoid simplifying away the learning goal.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the right support and observe whether it helps this class.

ambition.what: Offer a checked alternative explanation for learners who cannot access the original wording.

tasks.altitude: The teacher can prepare alternative versions faster, without delegating pupil assessment or live method changes.

reach.task: Review whether adapted material preserves access and challenge
reach.learn: Check scaffolds against the intended learning goal

evidence.claim: LessonUp’s editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.

assumptions: In s1 the teacher produces target_goal, desired reading level or scaffold, concepts_to_preserve and source_revision after inspecting work and discussion; its full 30% remains. No structured pupil-needs profile is assumed or sent to the assistant.
Use only approved source materials and omit pupil identifiers. Missing adaptation requirements are clarified manually before drafting.
Test an existing approved alternative and native editor before custom development. Only rewriting time changes; evaluation and live teaching remain unchanged.
unknowns: Whether the school has an approved editor and suitable existing alternatives
Which material types can be adapted without distorting concepts
research_questions: Across ten adaptations, how much rewriting time remains after checking concept preservation and classroom suitability?

already_counted.description: Compare draft and source for meaning and suitability

incremental.description: Maintain adaptation briefs and record failed transformations

approvals.approved_version: Teacher approves exact adapted-material revision against the source revision before student use; changed wording or source invalidates approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Provisional E1: B=100; R=30+17.5+35=82.5; gross=17.5%; minus 2 focal upkeep gives 15.5% net. Low: approved alternatives already exist or semantic repairs erase savings. High: rewriting is faster while identifying needs and live method adjustment retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Teachers can draft checked material alternatives faster while retaining instruction, encouragement and classroom decisions.
reach: Review accessible subject materials with special education colleagues
role.ambitious_version: Offer more suitable explanations without substituting generated text for classroom relationships or teacher judgement.

job.title: Secondary School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
